description: Contributor reputation on the Skill Hub. Single source of truth for tools/rep.py (registry.json `contributors`) and the 'How rep works' section of the /skills/scoring page. Identity is the GitHub login: the author namespace for published skills, the signed `verifier` principal for runs. There are no accounts and no seeded rep: every point comes from the registry build.

badges.label: Author
badges.description: Publishes at least one skill on the hub.

badges.label: Verifier
badges.description: At least one independent passing run of someone else's skill that counts.

badges.label: Device pioneer
badges.description: First to verify a skill on a device class nobody had covered for it.

badges.label: Maintainer
badges.description: Re-verifies other people's skills with a maintainer or platform key.

rules: Published: the sum of the current quality points of every skill in your author namespace. Deprecated skills earn nothing. Imported benchmark scaffolds (androidworld) have no human author and earn no rep.

Verified: points for each independent passing run of the current version of someone else's skill, counted the way the quality ladder counts it: one report per device fingerprint, never on a fingerprint the author recorded on, signed with your own key in SIGNERS.
Device pioneer bonus: the first independent passing run on a device class the skill had no independent pass on yet.
Bench model bonus: the first non-author passing run that carries a bench block for an agent model the author never benched this version with. The deterministic replay arm is not a model.

Maintained: a small fixed amount per skill of someone else's that you re-verified (maintainer or platform key, passing run of the current version). Your own runs of your own skills are self evidence and earn published points only through quality.
A new version resets run credit: only runs of the current version count, exactly like quality points.
Downloads, likes and stars are worth 0 rep.
Not enforced yet (planned): reciprocal verification caps, account age, random re-execution, decay.
